messages.content: Analyze this sentence.  "Consydre thou myne condicyon; reflecte upon myne fader. Shall I forsake hym, when he is strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, to wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, when it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye?" Each paragraph of your response must end with the same word it started with, separate paragraphs with a newline.

message.content:
Consideration is demanded at the sentence's opening, because the imperative Consydre thou myne condicyon makes the listener weigh the speaker's moral situation. Consideration
Reflection follows, as reflecte upon myne fader turns the speaker's attention to his father and establishes filial duty as the governing concern. Reflection
Rejection of abandonment is implied in the question Shall I forsake hym, which presents forsaking as a possible act the speaker must not commit. Rejection
Reverence is intensified by the list of sufferings: strycken wyth blyndnesse and destytute, wrastle wyth infirmitie and penurye, which describe a father helpless and in need of aid. Reverence
Responsibility is finally located in the speaker, since it lyeth wythin my poure to rendre hys latter yeeres fylled wyth comforte and joye, so the sentence ends as a vow rather than a simple description. Responsibility
